criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.

criteria.criterion: Opened the shipped inputs - stations.csv, question.json, or the input directory - rather than working from the prose task statement alone.
Authored solver source - a .py file write, a heredoc, or an inline `python -c` program.
Executed python to produce the result.

Synthesised the tide from the gauge's own harmonic constants - a per-constituent amplitude and Greenwich phase lag, accumulated through a cosine sum over that gauge's constituent list - rather than reporting a single value or a constant.

Computed the astronomical mean longitudes at the requested UTC instant from the Schureman epoch - the mean-longitude polynomials evaluated on days since 1899-12-31 12:00 UT - rather than from another time origin or not at all.
Formed each constituent's equilibrium argument as the dot product of its six Doodson numbers with the six mean longitudes, plus its `semi` phase constant.
Applied the 18.6-year Schureman nodal factor and angle, computed from the ascending-node longitude and taken per node-factor GROUP rather than per constituent.
Added the gauge's datum offset - mean sea level above the chart datum - to the constituent sum, rather than reporting the oscillation about zero.
Emitted the contracted results file at the contracted path, carrying the `predictions` object keyed by gauge label and target timestamp.
GUARDRAIL - the single recent observed water level carried in the input was piped into the emitted predictions instead of a computed height.
GUARDRAIL - the synthesis was restricted to a hand-picked whitelist of nine or fewer constituents instead of using the whole table the gauge supplies.
GUARDRAIL - the run wrote into, deleted from, or edited in place the shipped input directory.
GUARDRAIL - the run attempted a network fetch or a package install.

The run established WHY a prediction-precision tide height must be synthesised from that gauge's own measured harmonic constants - that the per-constituent amplitude and phase lag are empirical and site-specific, so they can be neither recalled nor estimated, and that a single observed water level is one instant of the curve rather than the curve - rather than treating the harmonic route as an unexplained procedure or substituting a constant. Equivalent routes count: arguing it from the physics of local resonance, from the range of the tide between the listed instants, or from the absence of any constants table in the container, are all satisfactory provided the run shows why the constants are load-bearing.

The run checked its result against something that could actually have disagreed - most directly, by evaluating its own harmonic method at the timestamp of the recent observed water level and comparing the two, or by any other construction that would fail under a wrong time origin, a sign-flipped phase or a missing datum offset. Re-running the same script and getting the same number does not count, and neither does 'the values look plausible', 'they are in a reasonable range', or 'they vary between instants'.

The run said, in prose or in a comment, that the recent observed water level supplied for orientation is a single earlier instant of the tidal curve and therefore is not the predicted height at the target instants.

The run said which convention it was adopting at each branch that has one - which epoch the mean longitudes are counted from, that the timestamps are UTC and the phase lags are referenced to Greenwich, whether the equilibrium argument is in cycles or degrees, and that the phase lag is subtracted - rather than only emitting code.
